thesis_summary.thesis: ASX Limited operates Australia's dominant market infrastructure: listings, cash-market trading, futures and over-the-counter clearing, settlement, registry, and market-data services. **[Fact]** Brokers, issuers, and clearing participants pay fees on activity; ASX does not take proprietary trading risk on its licensed market operations. **[Fact]** FY2025 (year ended 30 June 2025) operating revenue was **$1,107.2 million** (+7.0% versus **$1,034.3 million** in FY2024); underlying net profit after tax **$510.0 million** (+7.5%); underlying earnings per share **262.9 cents** (`investor-documents/official-reports/asx-2025-annual-report.pdf`). **[Fact]** Four reportable segments generated revenue: Listings **$208.0 million**, Markets **$349.2 million**, Technology & Data **$275.6 million**, and Securities & Payments **$274.4 million** (`investor-documents/official-reports/fy2025-results-market-announcement.pdf`). The group holds monopoly-style licences for Australia's primary exchange, clearing, and settlement facilities.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: There is no dated payoff or structural discount. **[Inference]** FY2025 benefited from solid growth across Markets (+10.7%), Technology & Data (+8.0%), and Securities & Payments (+7.4%), plus **$86.8 million** net interest income (+13.2%) on participant margin balances. **[Inference]** The market may correctly price regulatory and technology risk after the October 2024 CHESS batch settlement incident and the multi-year CHESS replacement program (**$77.7 million** of FY2025 capital spending). Return is franchise earnings power at price, not a mispricing with a known catalyst date.
